paper_metadata.title: Capturing dynamics with noisy quantum computers

summary: The paper studies parameterized quantum circuits for function approximation and generalization, proving universality results for Lp, C0, and Hk approximation under suitable normalization. Its numerical example trains a 3-layer PQC on the synthetic target f*(x)=x/(2π) using 10 training points, 100 epochs, and 100 repeated runs, comparing ℓ2 and ℓh1 losses under three normalization ranges: [-π/2, π/2], [-π, π], and [-2π, 2π].

experiments.description: Numerical experiment training a parameterized quantum circuit to approximate the linear function f*(x)=x/(2π) under different input normalizations and loss functions (ℓl2 vs ℓh1).

algorithm.variant: parameterized quantum circuit regression with data re-uploading
algorithm.ansatz: 3-layer circuit with alternating Rx(ωx) data-encoding and Ry(θ) trainable rotations; each qubit measured in Pauli-Z basis

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Input x is encoded through Rx(ωx) rotations; variational parameters are Ry(θij) rotations
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize regression loss between PQC output fθ(x) and target function f*(x)=x/(2π)

problem_instance.description: Approximation of a one-dimensional linear function on a bounded interval

dataset_specification.description: Target function f*(x)=x/(2π), x∈[-π,π]; training points uniformly distributed along the domain

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Min-max feature scaling / normalization to one of three intervals: [-π/2, π/2], [-π, π], or [-2π, 2π]
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Each experiment repeated 100 times; 25th, 50th, and 75th percentiles reported in figures

speedup_claims.caveats: This is an expressivity/generalization numerical study. No classical runtime or speedup comparison is reported.
